text: {"answer":"Evidence suggests intermittent fasting produces meaningful weight loss, but it is generally not superior to standard calorie restriction. A meta-analysis of randomized trials found intermittent energy restriction achieved comparable weight loss to continuous restriction (WMD -0.61 kg, non-significant) [e5aee0e45fc5#1]. A Harvard Nutrition Source summary of reviews likewise found no significant difference in weight loss or body composition between fasting and continuous calorie restriction groups [44e3472ec92d#6]. A systematic review reported that twelve studies comparing IF to calorie restriction found equivalent results [f781c705b786#2]. One meta-analysis reported a small, statistically significant extra body weight reduction with IF, though BMI did not differ [e5e8a6defcd9#1]. Dropout rates were not lower with fasting [44e3472ec92d#6]. Small trials combining fasting with calorie restriction also reported weight loss [23334c40ad6b#0]. Overall, intermittent fasting is an effective weight-loss option, roughly comparable to daily calorie restriction, with long-term trials still needed [e5aee0e45fc5#2].","confidence":72,"one_line":"Intermittent fasting produces weight loss comparable to continuous calorie restriction, though long-term evidence is still limited."}
